Diesel Generator (DG) sets are widely used for backup and continuous power supply in industries, commercial buildings, hospitals, and residential complexes. However, DG sets are also a significant source of air pollution. To address this issue, Emission Control Devices (ECDs) for DG Sets are used to reduce harmful exhaust emissions and ensure regulatory compliance.

This guide explains what an emission control device is, its types, uses, and advantages in a clear and beginner-friendly way.

What Is an Emission Control Device for DG Set?

An Emission Control Device (ECD) is a system installed on the exhaust of a diesel generator to reduce pollutants released into the atmosphere.

These devices help DG sets meet emission standards prescribed by pollution control authorities such as the Central Pollution Control Board and state pollution control boards.

Simply put, an emission control device makes a DG set cleaner, safer, and legally compliant.

Why Emission Control Devices Are Required for DG Sets

Diesel generators emit several harmful pollutants, including:

  • Particulate Matter (PM)
  • Nitrogen Oxides (NOx)
  • Carbon Monoxide (CO)
  • Hydrocarbons (HC)

These emissions contribute to respiratory problems, smog, and environmental degradation. Due to increasing air pollution, emission control devices have become mandatory for many existing DG sets in India.

Types of Emission Control Devices for DG Set

1. Filter-Based Emission Control Device

  • Uses physical filters to trap particulate matter
  • Effective in reducing smoke
  • Requires periodic cleaning or replacement

2. Filterless Emission Control Device

  • Uses catalytic or oxidation technology
  • Low maintenance
  • Longer operational life

3. Diesel Oxidation Catalyst (DOC)

  • Converts CO and hydrocarbons into less harmful gases
  • Often combined with other emission control systems

4. Retrofit Emission Control Device (RECD)

  • Installed on existing DG sets
  • Helps older generators comply with current emission norms
  • Widely adopted due to cost-effectiveness

Uses of Emission Control Devices for DG Set

Emission control devices are used in:

  • Industrial plants and factories
  • Hospitals and healthcare facilities
  • Commercial buildings and malls
  • Data centers
  • Residential societies
  • Construction sites

Anywhere a diesel generator is used, an emission control device helps reduce pollution and ensure compliance.

Advantages of Emission Control Device for DG Set

Installing an emission control device offers multiple benefits:

  • Compliance with pollution control norms
  • Significant reduction in smoke and particulate matter
  • Improved local air quality
  • Avoidance of fines, penalties, and DG set shutdown
  • Environment-friendly operations
  • Extended life of existing DG sets
  • No need for expensive DG set replacement

Is an Emission Control Device Mandatory for DG Sets?

Yes. For many existing and older DG sets, emission control devices are mandatory under current pollution control regulations. Authorities may issue notices, impose fines, or restrict operation of non-compliant DG sets.

Installing a certified emission control device ensures smooth and legal operation.

Conclusion

An Emission Control Device for DG Set is an essential solution to manage diesel generator pollution. With different types available-filter-based, filterless, catalytic, and retrofit-these devices help reduce harmful emissions, protect public health, and ensure regulatory compliance.

For DG set owners, installing an emission control device is not just a legal requirement but also a responsible step toward cleaner air and sustainable power usage.
